title: Watchtower: tenant-aware rapid remediation for canary regressions across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: We have recurring cases where canary regressions surface only for a subset of tenant slices (subscriber-heavy customers) and the current rollback procedures are manual, slow, and risk leaving KV cache inconsistencies across environments (hosted/dedicated/private). This ticket scopes building a 'Watchtower' remediation orchestration and on-call runbook to accelerate safe rollbacks or targeted remediation while preserving customer continuity.

Goals:
- Automate detection-to-remediation flow for canary failures that affect high-value tenant slices (subscriber-facing regressions).
- Provide tenant-aware rollback choreography that can execute: global rollback, tenant-slice pin, or staged rollforward with livepatch where safe.
- Reconcile KV cache and prefix caches across affected nodes (avoid stale caches causing split-brain responses).
- Ensure coordinated customer communication pathways and runbook actions for oncall and SEs.
- Maintain clear audit trail (PR, rollout IDs, tenant lists) and postmortem data for quality regressions.

Scope and non-goals:
- Includes new orchestration lambda + controller changes to runtime routing.
- Adds onboarded checks in Console for Watchtower alerts and tenant-slice filters.
- Does NOT include full private air-gapped automation for every customer; private mode will get a semi-automated play that requires operator approval due to KMS/network isolation.

Key components to deliver:
1) Detection ruleset: combined signal of generation quality regression (eval metric deltas), latency spike (p50/p95 delta), and error-rate uptick. Allow per-tenant thresholds.
2) Remediation engine: three action types: rollback-to-pin, slice-quarantine (route to fallback model variant), livepatch-hotfix (config-only fixes). Each action includes preflight checks and rollback handshake.
3) KV cache reconciler: a safe-step plan to drain, snapshot, and reconcile KV stores for tenants moved between model variants to avoid incoherent responses.
4) Orchestration UI flows: Console panel for Watchtower incidents with tenant lists, action buttons (CanaryQuarantine / PinVersion / Rollback), and RSVP logging.
5) Runbook & oncall commands: documented cli and playbook that SREs and SEs can follow; include templates for external customer comms.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: unsafe automated rollback could worsen regressions for other tenants. Mitigation: default to 'suggested action' requiring one human approval for cross-deployment rollbacks; allow fully-automated for low-impact tenants only.
- Risk: KV reconciliation may be slow for large tenant state. Mitigation: implement incremental snapshot + tombstone propagation and provide estimated duration to oncall.
- Risk: Private deployments have network/KMS restrictions. Mitigation: require operator approval and provide an operator-facing checklist.

acceptance_criteria: Watchtower detection rule deployed to staging and firing on synthetic canary failure signals
Remediation engine can execute a tenant-pin and tenant-quarantine action in staging without human error
KV cache reconciler demonstrates consistent responses for moved tenants in a staged test (latency within SLOs)
Console shows Watchtower incident with tenant list and action buttons; actions log rollout IDs
Oncall runbook published and validated by SRE with at least one tabletop drill
